title: Misleading precedence rule triggered intermittent model-flavor handshake loop
creator: Ethan Park
description: Customer-facing incidents (intermittent 503s and elevated tail latency mid-Feb to early Mar) were traced to the routing policy precedence inversion combined with stale per-route preference caches. Under specific load patterns, requests repeatedly toggled between a low-latency regional variant and a lower-capacity cross-region model-flavor, leading to a handshake loop that amplified capacity pressure and caused cascading throttles.
timeline: 2026-03-02 10:12 UTC - First customer ticket reports intermittent timeouts for chat generation in EU region.
2026-03-02 11:00 UTC - On-call routed to serving-runtime team; initial hypothesis: transient GPU exhaustion due to a traffic spike.
2026-03-02 14:40 UTC - Telemetry shows increased cross-region egress from EU->US during the spike window; spike correlates with model-flavor selection changes.

2026-03-03 02:20 UTC - Debugging session: observed policy evaluation logs where precedence rules returned non-deterministic ordering for two compatible variants (regional-fast vs cross-region-high-capacity).

2026-03-04 09:10 UTC - Reproduced handshake loop in local staging simulation by replaying production routing events; loop required three conditions: (1) policy precedence inversion on concurrent policy update, (2) per-route preference cache TTL misalignment across routers, (3) soft-fallback threshold that considered a stale success sample as valid.
2026-03-04 13:35 UTC - Emergency mitigation deployed: increase preference cache TTL normalization and apply short-lived sticky route suppression during policy rollouts.
2026-03-05 07:00 UTC - Traffic and error rates returned to baseline. Begin formal post-incident analysis.
2026-03-09 16:00 UTC - Draft postmortem completed; engineering and product reviews requested.
2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - Action items prioritized and assigned. In Review status for follow-up PRs and console changes.
root_cause: An interaction bug in the routing policy evaluator produced a non-deterministic precedence order when two rules had overlapping selectors and nearly-equal weights during a concurrent policy change. This was compounded by per-route preference caches on edge routers having TTLs that drifted during rolling config updates, causing routers to consult stale preference values and emit routing decisions that triggered cross-region failovers. The soft-fallback logic treated a single stale success sample as fully healthy, enabling a two-way oscillation (handshake loop) under load.
mitigations: Immediate: Temporarily suppressed sticky fallbacks during active policy rollouts (deployed 2026-03-04 13:35 UTC).
Immediate: Normalized preference cache TTLs across routers and invalidated caches for affected routes (2026-03-04 13:50 UTC).
Short-term: Added additional logging at policy-evaluation hot path to capture precedence decisions and sample provenance for every route decision.
Medium-term: Implement deterministic tie-breaker in policy evaluator (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/route-eval/pull/459).

Medium-term: Harden soft-fallback heuristics to require sustained degradation samples before initiating variant switch (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REINF/soft-fallback-hardening).
Long-term: Introduce a rollout-aware router mode that suppresses aggressive retries and sticky switching while policy propagation completes (target release runtime-1.20).
Long-term: Add an automated canary checker that validates policy precedence convergence across regions before allowing rollouts to proceed.
